title: How Pac-Man got his name
hook: Pac-Man was named after a Japanese sound for eating, and nearly something else.
peek: Pac-Man's name comes from paku paku, a Japanese word for the sound of a mouth opening and closing. In Japan he launched as Puck Man, a name that was changed before the game reached American arcades.
lede: Toru Iwatani designed Pac-Man at Namco, and it reached Japanese arcades in 1980. The name comes from paku paku, a Japanese expression for the sound and motion of a mouth opening and closing as it eats. Iwatani wanted a game built around eating rather than shooting, so he named his hero after the one thing he does.

bullets.text: At home the game launched as Puck Man, a spelling of pakku-man, roughly the chomping man. The yellow hero is little more than a mouth, so the name describes him exactly.
For the American release the distributor, Midway, changed the name to Pac-Man. The usual explanation is that it feared vandals would scratch the P on arcade cabinets into an F.
Iwatani has said the shape came partly from a pizza with one slice missing, and partly from rounding off the Japanese character for mouth. The pizza half is the version most often retold.
The four ghosts got names too. In Japan their nicknames describe how they move, such as chaser and ambusher. English players know them as Blinky, Pinky, Inky and Clyde.
